obligation: Oil discharge notice to the National Response Center
trigger: Discharge of oil in a quantity that may be harmful (40 CFR 110.3: violates water quality standards or causes a film or sheen on the water or adjoining shorelines), for example a tank overflow or flow line release caused by loss of SCADA control
deadline: Immediately, as soon as the person in charge has knowledge
notify: National Response Center (800-424-8802); if not practicable, the Coast Guard or EPA on-scene coordinator
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - if a release reaches water; HSE and Regulatory Manager decides

trigger: Unauthorized access to electronic personal information of Florida residents (royalty owners: names with Social Security numbers; employees: Social Security, driver license, health plan numbers, or geolocation)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred; delay only on written law enforcement request; no notice if a documented, counsel-supported no-harm determination is made (send it to the department within 30 days; keep 5 years)
notify: Each affected Florida resident (mail or email)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - if personal information was accessed

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (15 more days for individual notice if good cause is given in writing within the 30 days)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - if 500 or more Florida residents (about 2,300 royalty owners could be affected)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time

obligation: Vendor breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A third-party agent (production accounting, HR and payroll, telematics vendor) has a breach of a system it maintains for the company
deadline: Vendor must notify the company no later than 10 days after determination; the company then gives the (3) and (4) notices

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Royalty owners or employees who reside outside Florida are affected
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Residents and regulators per each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - many royalty owners live outside Florida; counsel applies the law of each state where affected individuals reside

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA

obligation: Voluntary report to CISA and the FBI
citation: No legal requirement for this company (see CIRCIA row); CISA and FBI reporting channels
trigger: Ransomware or any intrusion into SCADA
deadline: As soon as practicable; the runbook targets day 0 to 1
notify: CISA (cisa.gov/report or 844-729-2472); FBI field office or IC3
applies_at_this_tier: Voluntary - recommended; supports the OFAC mitigating factor and sector warning

deadline: Per policy (use the carrier's breach hotline before hiring vendors)

citation: Crude purchase contract; gas purchase contract; joint operating agreements; reserve-based credit agreement (contracts)
trigger: Incident that stops deliveries or affects partner or lender data
deadline: Per each contract (force majeure notices; lender notice of material adverse events)
notify: Crude purchaser; gas gathering company; non-operating partners; lender
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual; CFO checks each contract with counsel

obligation: Reporting of actual or threatened cyber incidents at MTSA facilities / OCS facilities / vessels
trigger: Cyber incident involving or endangering a vessel, harbor, port, or waterfront facility
deadline: Immediately (6.16-1); 'without delay' to the National Response Center for entities not reporting under 6.16-1
notify: FBI, CISA (for any cyber incident), and the Coast Guard Captain of the Port; or National Response Center
applies_at_this_tier: No - onshore only; no vessel, waterfront facility, or OCS facility (N21-R01 not applicable, P03)

trigger: Cybersecurity incident at a TSA-notified pipeline owner or operator
deadline: As soon as practicable, but no later than 72 hours after identifying a cybersecurity incident
notify: CISA Central (cisa.gov/report or 844-729-2472); CISA shares with TSA
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company operates no pipeline and has no TSA notice (N21-R02 not applicable, P03)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident report / ransom payment report (PROPOSED - not yet in effect)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment by a covered entity
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours after reasonable belief a covered cyber incident occurred; 24 hours after ransom payment disbursed
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; as proposed, the company is below the SBA size standard and meets no sector criterion (P03 G-115); recheck when final

citation: FAR 52.204-25 (Section 889) and FAR 52.204-23; FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Covered equipment or Kaspersky covered article identified in contract performance
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
